item.title: Your Gemini Gems stop working today
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Gems on personal Google accounts are now read-only. You can open them, but you cannot use, edit or create them. On December 17, Google removes them for good. Google says it will turn your Gems into skills automatically. Skills are saved instructions you call with a slash and their name. Download Gem knowledge files before December 17. Skills do not work with Canvas or Deep Research yet. Sources: Google Gemini Help, Google Blog, MIXED, The Decoder.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"Gemini Gems become read-only as Google moves users to skills","dek":"Personal account Gems can no longer be used or edited from November 17, 2026, and Google plans to remove them on December 17.","summary":"Google's Gemini Gems on personal accounts became read-only on November 17, 2026, and will be removed on December 17, 2026. Google says it will convert existing Gems into skills automatically, but some file types and features do not carry over.","seo_title":"Gemini Gems read-only: what changes and when they go away","seo_description":"Gemini Gems turned read-only on November 17, 2026 and will be removed December 17. Google removes them on December 17, 2026, and converts them into skills automatically.","tags":["Google","Gemini","Gems","Gemini skills"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Google's Gemini Gems, the custom assistants people set up with their own instructions and files, became read-only on personal Google accounts on November 17, 2026. According to Google's Gemini help center, users can still open their Gems but can no longer use them, edit them or create new ones. Google plans to remove them entirely on December 17, 2026.","sources":[{"name":"Google Gemini Help","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/18560919"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The change is the final stage of a plan Google announced on September 30, 2026, when it introduced skills in the Gemini app and said they would replace Gems as the main way to tailor Gemini to a specific task. The company said at the time that it would migrate existing Gems into skills automatically when Gems went away.","sources":[{"name":"Google Blog","url":"https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/automate-tasks-with-skills/"},{"name":"The Decoder","url":"https://the-decoder.com/google-drops-gems-for-skills-joining-openai-and-anthropic-in-the-shift-to-agent-ready-prompt-formats/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How skills differ from Gems","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Skills are saved sets of instructions that a user calls up by typing a forward slash and the skill's name in the prompt bar. Google says Gemini can also create a skill from an earlier chat and run it automatically when a matching request appears. Several skills can be combined in one conversation, and a skill can hold reference files such as text documents, PDFs and images.","sources":[{"name":"Google Blog","url":"https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/automate-tasks-with-skills/"},{"name":"MIXED","url":"https://mixed-news.com/en/gemini-gems-removed-november-skills-canvas-deep-research/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Skills use the open SKILL.md format, which The Decoder noted originated with Anthropic. Users can create as many skills as they want, but only 100 can be active at the same time, according to Google's help center and MIXED.","sources":[{"name":"Google Gemini Help","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/18560919"},{"name":"MIXED","url":"https://mixed-news.com/en/gemini-gems-removed-november-skills-canvas-deep-research/"},{"name":"The Decoder","url":"https://the-decoder.com/google-drops-gems-for-skills-joining-openai-and-anthropic-in-the-shift-to-agent-ready-prompt-formats/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What does not carry over","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google's help center says skills do not yet work with Canvas, Deep Research, video creation, music creation or Guided Learning, all features that worked inside Gems. Each skill has a 100 MB limit for files, and Google says it removes the largest files first when a converted Gem exceeds that limit. GitHub files, audio, video, older Office formats such as .doc, .xls and .ppt, and compressed archives do not transfer.","sources":[{"name":"Google Gemini Help","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/18560919"},{"name":"MIXED","url":"https://mixed-news.com/en/gemini-gems-removed-november-skills-canvas-deep-research/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google advises users to download knowledge files from their Gems before December 17, 2026. Users who do not want to wait for the automatic conversion can rebuild a Gem by hand from the Skills page by copying its name, description and instructions into a new skill. Sharing permissions on a Gem carry over to the skill, and Gems shared by others appear on the Skills page as inactive until the user accepts them.","sources":[{"name":"Google Gemini Help","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/18560919"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Gems made by Google Labs and the Opal mini app builder were also turned off on November 17, 2026, and they do not convert into skills, MIXED reported. Opal workflow files remain in an Opal folder in the owner's Google Drive.","sources":[{"name":"Google Blog","url":"https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/automate-tasks-with-skills/"},{"name":"MIXED","url":"https://mixed-news.com/en/gemini-gems-removed-november-skills-canvas-deep-research/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Dates for other accounts","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The November and December dates apply to personal accounts of users 18 and older. Google Workspace business, enterprise and nonprofit accounts keep Gems until March 2027, and education accounts until June 2027. Google has not yet given a date for personal accounts of users under 18.","sources":[{"name":"Google Gemini Help","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/18560919"},{"name":"Google Blog","url":"https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/automate-tasks-with-skills/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"For most people the switch should be quiet, because the conversion is automatic. The real cost falls on users whose Gems depended on Canvas, Deep Research or large file libraries, since those parts will not behave the same way after the move.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"December 17, 2026 is the date to watch: after it, Gem knowledge files that were not downloaded or converted will no longer be available.","sources":[]}]}

item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Sign in on the web or the app, then browse characters other users made, from heroes to quirky personalities. Talk by text, or switch to a live voice call. item.title: n8n vs Zapier: which one to use for AI automation
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Zapier bills one task per action step that runs. Triggers, filters and paths are free. n8n counts one execution per workflow run, however many steps it has. Zapier lists 9,000+ apps and a Copilot that builds Zaps from plain English. n8n has fewer apps and a steeper learning curve. Some steps need code. Sources: Zapier: Zapier vs. n8n comparison, n8n: Plans and pricing, n8n Docs: Executions, Zapier: Zapier pricing, Zapier: What is a task in Zapier?, Dupple: n8n pricing 2026, Jet Admin: n8n vs Zapier in 2026.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"n8n vs Zapier: which automation tool to use for AI workflows","dek":"Zapier is the easy, managed option with the bigger app catalog. n8n is cheaper for long workflows and can run on your own server, but it asks more of you.","summary":"Zapier bills one task for each action step that runs, while n8n bills one execution for each full workflow run. Zapier connects more apps and is easier to learn; n8n can be self-hosted and leans on code for complex work.","seo_title":"n8n vs Zapier: which automation tool for AI workflows","seo_description":"n8n vs Zapier compared for AI workflows: how each bills (tasks vs executions), plan prices, self-hosting, AI agent features and which one fits you.","answer_summary":"Pick Zapier if you want the fastest setup, the most app connections and no servers. Pick n8n if your workflows have many steps, you want to self-host, or you are comfortable with some JavaScript.","tags":["n8n","Zapier","Automation","AI agents","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"n8n vs Zapier is the first choice most people face when they want AI inside their automations. Both connect apps and both can add AI steps and agents to a workflow. The big differences are how they bill, where they run and how much technical work they expect from you. Zapier is a fully managed cloud service. n8n can run in its own cloud or on a server you control.","sources":[{"name":"Zapier: Zapier vs. n8n comparison","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/n8n-vs-zapier/"},{"name":"Jet Admin: n8n vs Zapier in 2026","url":"https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/n8n-vs-zapier/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"This guide uses each company's own pricing and documentation, plus two independent pricing breakdowns from the fall of 2026. One caution: the main comparison page used here is published by Zapier, so read its claims about n8n with that in mind. Prices change and can show in your local currency, so check the pricing page before you pay.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"n8n vs Zapier: the short answer","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Use Zapier if you want something working in an afternoon, need an app that only Zapier supports, or nobody on your team wants to look at code. Use n8n if your workflows run many steps many times a day, you need your data on your own servers, or you already write some JavaScript. For a few small automations, both free options are enough to decide.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Tasks vs executions: how each one bills","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Zapier defines a task as anything it successfully completes for you, and a task only happens when an action step runs. Triggers, polling checks and failed steps do not count. Filter, Formatter and Paths steps are also free.","sources":[{"name":"Zapier: What is a task in Zapier?","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/what-is-a-task-in-zapier/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"n8n's docs define an execution as a single run of a workflow. Only production runs count toward a plan's limit: runs started by a trigger, a schedule or a polling node. Manual test runs, sub-workflow calls and error workflow runs do not count. A polling node counts only when it finds new data, while a Schedule Trigger counts every time it fires.","sources":[{"name":"n8n Docs: Executions","url":"https://docs.n8n.io/workflows/executions/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"In practice, a Zap with one trigger and four action steps that runs 1,000 times uses up to 4,000 tasks. The same workflow in n8n is 1,000 executions. The longer your workflows, the bigger that gap gets, which is why AI workflows with many steps tend to cost less on n8n.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the plans cost","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Zapier's Free plan includes 100 tasks a month. Professional costs $19.99 a month billed annually and starts at 750 tasks, with multi-step Zaps, premium apps, Filters, Paths and Formatter. Team costs $69 a month billed annually and adds shared folders, shared app connections, user roles and SAML SSO. Enterprise is custom. Copilot is on every plan.","sources":[{"name":"Zapier: Zapier pricing","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/zapier-pricing/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Jet Admin's comparison notes that Zapier's free plan is limited to two-step Zaps. On paid plans, Zapier keeps running past your limit and bills extra tasks at the end of the cycle: 1.25 times the normal task cost on annual plans and 2.5 times on monthly plans. At 3 times your plan's limit, your Zaps pause until the next billing cycle or an upgrade.","sources":[{"name":"Zapier: What is a task in Zapier?","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/what-is-a-task-in-zapier/"},{"name":"Jet Admin: n8n vs Zapier in 2026","url":"https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/n8n-vs-zapier/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"n8n Cloud Starter costs 20 a month billed annually, with 2,500 executions and 5 concurrent executions. Pro costs 50 a month billed annually, with 10,000 executions. n8n says every plan includes unlimited users, unlimited workflows and every integration. Dupple lists these prices in US dollars and notes that monthly billing costs more than yearly.","sources":[{"name":"n8n: Plans and pricing","url":"https://n8n.io/pricing/"},{"name":"Dupple: n8n pricing 2026","url":"https://dupple.com/learn/n8n-pricing"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The self-hosted Community edition of n8n costs nothing in license fees and has no plan quota, according to Dupple. You still pay for the server and for the work of updates, backups and security patches. It runs under n8n's Sustainable Use License, which allows internal business use but not reselling n8n to clients.","sources":[{"name":"Dupple: n8n pricing 2026","url":"https://dupple.com/learn/n8n-pricing"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Before you compare prices, count the steps in the workflow you actually plan to run and how often it fires. That one number usually decides the cheaper tool.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Ease of use and app connections","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Zapier says it connects more than 9,000 apps, all maintained by Zapier, and that n8n has about a quarter as many, many of them maintained by the community with irregular update schedules. Jet Admin describes Zapier's linear builder as easier for people who do not think in graphs, while n8n's node canvas rewards technical users.","sources":[{"name":"Zapier: Zapier vs. n8n comparison","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/n8n-vs-zapier/"},{"name":"Jet Admin: n8n vs Zapier in 2026","url":"https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/n8n-vs-zapier/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"n8n lets you add JavaScript and Python code nodes anywhere in a workflow. Zapier's own comparison says that to get the most out of n8n there is no real way around writing code. Zapier offers Code by Zapier for the same kind of custom logic, but most Zaps never need it.","sources":[{"name":"Zapier: Zapier vs. n8n comparison","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/n8n-vs-zapier/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"AI features in each","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Zapier's AI tools include Copilot, which builds workflows from a plain-language request, AI steps inside Zaps, Zapier MCP, which connects AI tools like Claude and ChatGPT to its apps, AI Guardrails and human-in-the-loop steps. You can pick a default, advanced or premium model, or bring your own key.","sources":[{"name":"Zapier: Zapier vs. n8n comparison","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/n8n-vs-zapier/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On Zapier, an AI step costs tasks like any other action: one task with the default model, three with Advanced and five with Premium. n8n offers AI Agent, MCP and human-in-the-loop nodes and a framework for evaluating agents. Its Cloud plans include Assistant credits, 1,600 a month on Starter, which n8n counts separately from executions.","sources":[{"name":"Zapier: Zapier pricing","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/zapier-pricing/"},{"name":"Zapier: Zapier vs. n8n comparison","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/n8n-vs-zapier/"},{"name":"n8n: Plans and pricing","url":"https://n8n.io/pricing/"},{"name":"Jet Admin: n8n vs Zapier in 2026","url":"https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/n8n-vs-zapier/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Which one to pick","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. You want it working today","text":"Pick Zapier. Start on the Free plan, describe your workflow to Copilot and check the result. Move to Professional when you need more than two steps.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Your workflows are long or run often","text":"Pick n8n. Count your steps and runs, then compare n8n's execution limits with the tasks the same work would use on Zapier.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Your data must stay on your servers","text":"Pick self-hosted n8n, and make sure someone owns updates, backups and security. Zapier has no self-hosted option.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"What each is bad at: Zapier gets expensive as steps and AI calls add up, and you cannot host it yourself. n8n asks for more setup, more code and more upkeep, its app catalog is smaller, and Starter's limit of 5 concurrent runs can bite before the execution count does.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Siri AI is getting a daily limit
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The iOS, iPadOS and macOS 27.3 betas give each device a daily allowance for advanced Siri requests, image tools and cloud model Shortcuts. item.title: How to use Napkin AI to turn text into visuals
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Open a new napkin and paste your text, or import a PPT, DOC, PDF or Markdown file. Write it like you would explain it out loud. Hover over a paragraph, click the spark, and pick from several visuals built from your words. Numbered steps become flowcharts. Change words, colors, icons and layout. Free plan: PNG and PDF with Napkin branding, 500 credits a week. Check every arrow: it can draw links your text never made. Sources: Napkin AI, Napkin AI pricing, Fast.io: Napkin AI review 2026, Turn Text Into Visuals: Getting Started With Napkin AI, The Windows Club: How to use Napkin AI.

item.title: The real Wolf of Wall Street just launched an AI voice that sells like he does
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Tone adjusts volume, speed, pacing and emphasis to the goal of a conversation, like a calmer voice for an angry caller. It is built on Belfort's Straight Line sales method and a patent granted in October 2025. Belfort says Tone could catch top salespeople within six months to a year, but admits it is not there yet. He says it has raised about $10 million and calls only opted-in leads. Sources: TokenPost, Business Wire, Dealroom, Superpower Daily.

item.title: OpenAI just let outside auditors inside its labs
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Apollo Research, METR, Transluce and Goodfire signed on for what OpenAI calls embedded assessments. They get selected internal models, training records and safety systems. Some can interview employees. Apollo sends six researchers for four months to test whether training teaches models to deceive. METR reviews OpenAI's largest reinforcement learning run yet. Transluce checks if safety tests catch score gaming. Sources: The Neuron, Superpower Daily, 36Kr.

If you only have a personal Google account, read the section on Antigravity CLI at the end first.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What you need before you install Gemini CLI","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The official docs list macOS 15 or later, Windows 11 24H2 or later, or Ubuntu 20.04 or later. You need Node.js 20.0.0 or newer, a Bash, Zsh or PowerShell shell, and an internet connection. Google suggests 4GB of RAM for short sessions and 16GB or more for long sessions on large codebases. Set GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT and GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION, sign in with gcloud auth application-default login, or use a service account key or a Google Cloud API key, then pick Vertex AI when gemini starts.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini CLI docs: Authentication","url":"https://www.geminicli.com/docs/get-started/authentication"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Treat the API key like a password. Philipp Schmid's cheatsheet notes that it respects .gitignore and .geminiignore. Start a line with ! to run a shell command, or type ! on its own to switch into shell mode.","sources":[{"name":"Philipp Schmid: Gemini CLI cheatsheet","url":"https://www.philschmid.de/gemini-cli-cheatsheet"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Run /init to create a starting GEMINI.md file. That file holds your project's rules, such as which test command to use or which folders to leave alone. A global file at ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md applies to every project, and /memory show prints the combined context the model actually receives.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini CLI docs: Cheatsheet","url":"https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/cli-reference.md"},{"name":"Philipp Schmid: Gemini CLI cheatsheet","url":"https://www.philschmid.de/gemini-cli-cheatsheet"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Use /stats model to see your token use and remaining quota, /chat save with a tag to keep a conversation, and /quit to leave. Short, specific rules work better than a long essay.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Gemini CLI falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google's own docs say Gemini CLI has not been optimized for Gemini 4 Argon and point users of that model to Antigravity. In a test on the June shutdown day, The New Stack hit repeated HTTP 503 high demand errors with Gemini CLI, and automatic retries ate into the free quota until the tester turned on billing. In that test, non-interactive mode could not write files or run shell commands.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini CLI docs: Installation","url":"https://www.geminicli.com/docs/get-started/installation"},{"name":"The New Stack: Gemini CLI vs. Antigravity","url":"https://thenewstack.io/gemini-cli-antigravity-replacement/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The approval mode setting decides how much it does without asking. The choices are default, auto_edit, yolo and plan. Yolo approves every action automatically, so keep it for throwaway folders.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini CLI docs: Cheatsheet","url":"https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/cli-reference.md"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"If you are a free or AI Pro user: Antigravity CLI","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google moved personal accounts to Antigravity CLI, a closed source Go program started with the agy command. Google says Agent Skills, Hooks, Subagents and Extensions carry over, and the official migration guide with an FAQ is at antigravity.google/docs/gcli-migration. The New Stack found that its Gemini extensions imported and ran as skills, while a simple single file custom command did not.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini CLI on GitHub: Transitioning Gemini CLI to Antigravity CLI","url":"https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/discussions/27274"},{"name":"The New Stack","url":"https://thenewstack.io/google-antigravity-cli/"},{"name":"The New Stack: Gemini CLI vs. Antigravity","url":"https://thenewstack.io/gemini-cli-antigravity-replacement/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The short version: Gemini CLI is still a solid, open source agent if you reach it through work, Google Cloud or a paid API key. For a personal account, install Antigravity CLI instead, and keep Gemini CLI for the projects where your company pays.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Trump is about to crown America's AI national champions
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The Trump administration plans to name more than two dozen US companies as AI national champions, The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday. Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic are on the list. Chosen firms would bundle US chips, AI models and cloud into packages that are easy for foreign buyers. In return: faster export licenses, government advocacy abroad and federal financing. The aim is to get foreign governments to pick American AI over Chinese rivals like Huawei. Sources: The Next Web, Open Magazine, Coinpedia.

item.title: Alibaba's new AI cuts task costs by 62 percent
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On Alibaba's own Work360 test, the average task cost dropped from $4.43 to $1.67 compared with Qwen3.8-Max. API prices: $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens. It has a 2.4 trillion parameter backbone and a 1 million token context window. On Terminal-Bench 4.0 it scored 48.5, behind Kimi K3.1 at 67.2 and Opus 5.5 at 59.6, by Alibaba's own numbers. Sources: ShiftDelete.Net, Lapaas Voice, RuntimeWire.

item.title: Apple's first smart glasses run on Siri and your iPhone, and could arrive in 2027
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Code-named N50, the glasses have cameras but no AR display. Siri uses the cameras to answer questions about what is around you. Open Text to Speech","text":"Sign in and select Text to Speech in the sidebar. This is the main screen where you type or paste your script and choose the voice.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Pick a voice and the model","text":"Choose a voice from the list and set the model to Eleven v4 unless you have a reason not to. Listen to a couple of voices with a short line first. A voice that fits the tone of your script saves you more retries than any setting.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Paste your script","text":"Keep each generation under the limit: 10,000 characters on v4, 5,000 on the others. If your script is longer, split it at natural breaks like the end of a paragraph so the pacing stays even when you join the parts.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Add direction with audio tags","text":"Eleven v4 and v3 understand short instructions in square brackets. Put the tag right where the delivery should change. ElevenLabs lists emotions like [curious], [crying] and [mischievously], delivery tags like [whispers] and [shouts], and human reactions like [laughs], [clears throat] and [sighs]. The same tags work on both models.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Script example 1: a calm explainer with one surprise","text":"[curious] Have you ever wondered where your old phone goes after you trade it in?
Most people never ask. [whispers] The answer is stranger than you think.
[clears throat] Let's start at the store counter.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Script example 2: a short ad read","text":"[mischievously] It's here. The new [product name] is finally out.
[sighs] We know, you've waited a long time.
[laughs] It was worth it. Go to [your website] to see it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Add pauses the right way","text":"Eleven v4 and v3 do not support SSML break tags, so control pacing with tags and punctuation. A single hyphen often adds a short pause and two in a row add a longer one. An ellipsis also adds a pause, but it can make the voice sound hesitant or nervous. On Multilingual v2, Flash v2 and Flash v2.5 you can use a break tag instead, up to 3 seconds long.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Break tag for Multilingual v2 and Flash models","text":""Give me one second to think about it." <break time="1.0s" /> "Yes, that would work."","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Don't stack breaks. ElevenLabs says many break tags in one text can make the speech speed up or add noise, and some voices fill a long pause with an "uh" or "ah".","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Fix words it says wrong","text":"The simplest fix works on every model: respell the word the way it sounds. ElevenLabs suggests capital letters, hyphens, apostrophes or single quotes around a few letters to push the stress, for example writing trapezii as trapezIi. On Flash v2 and Turbo v2 you can use SSML phoneme tags with IPA or CMU spelling, and Eleven v3 understands IPA directly.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Generate, then use your free retries","text":"Every click on Generate uses credits, including after you edit the text. But on the website you get two free regenerations as long as the text, the voice and the model stay the same, the first take was less than two hours ago and you have not refreshed or left the page. You can still move the voice sliders between those retries. On v3, each click gives you two takes for the price of one.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"8. Download the file","text":"Click the download button at the bottom right as soon as the audio is made. To get an older file, open the history tab in the right side panel of Text to Speech and click the download icon. The default choices are MP3 at 128 kbps or WAV. Under Advanced you can pick MP3 at 192 or 256 kbps, M4A or FLAC.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What ElevenLabs is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The free plan is good for testing voices and making audio for yourself, not for a channel that earns money, since commercial use needs a paid plan. Ten minutes of audio a month also goes quickly if you retry a lot, so get the script right before you press Generate and lean on the two free retries instead of editing and starting over. Pronunciation of rare names still needs hand fixing, and v4 drops the Style and Speed sliders that some people used on older models.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Before you spend credits on a long script, test the voice, the model and your tags on two or three sentences. When that short test sounds right, paste the rest.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: ChatGPT vs Claude: which one to use for what
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: ChatGPT Plus and Claude Pro both cost $20 a month. ChatGPT also has Go at $8. Claude Pro drops to $17 a month if you pay for a year. item.title: Claude built a whole swimmable ocean, kelp forests and a shipwreck, in one file of just 97 KB
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Abyssal Garden is a single HTML file of about 97 KB. It has no images, no 3D models, no sound files and no game engine. Every kelp leaf, rock and fish is generated by code when the page opens. The seabed is sculpted on the graphics card, then filled with about two million kelp leaves and plants and thousands of fish and corals. The developer reports about 180 FPS at 1440p on an RTX 5070 Ti. The prompt banned game engines and set up a second AI agent that only saw screenshots and reported visual flaws. Sources: Wccftech, XDA Developers, Abyssal Garden on GitHub.

item.title: How to use Claude Cowork to hand off a whole task
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Open Claude on the web, desktop or phone, pick Cowork in the message box and say what you want done. Review its plan, then let it run. Connect folders on desktop, and apps through the + menu or Customize, Connectors. Claude only sees the folders you connect. Type /schedule in a task, or open Scheduled in the sidebar. Scheduled tasks run in the cloud, even when your computer is off. Sources: Claude Help Center: Get started with Claude Cowork, Claude Help Center: Use Cowork on web, desktop and mobile, Claude: Cowork product page, TechRadar: Claude Cowork expands to mobile and web.

Credits are charged per minute of the original video you import, not per clip you get back. A 30 minute podcast costs 30 credits whether it produces 5 clips or 20. Partial minutes round down, so a 4.5 minute video counts as 4, but anything under a minute still costs 1 credit.","sources":[{"name":"OpusClip Help Center: How are credits consumed","url":"https://help.opus.pro/docs/article/how-are-credits-consumed"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On monthly plans, credits expire after 60 days, so unused credits roll over for one extra month. Yearly plans get the full year of credits up front. On the free plan, the pricing page says clips can no longer be exported after 3 days, so download what you want soon after it is made.","sources":[{"name":"OpusClip Help Center: How are credits consumed","url":"https://help.opus.pro/docs/article/how-are-credits-consumed"},{"name":"OpusClip: Pricing","url":"https://opus.pro/pricing"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use the Processing timeframe slider to process only the part of the video you care about. Add your video","text":"Sign in and paste a video link or upload a file. Free accounts can use YouTube links and local files. Starter adds Google Drive, Vimeo, Zoom, Rumble and StreamYard. OpusClip says it supports videos up to 10 hours long.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Choose the clip model","text":"Under Clip model, select ClipAnything. OpusClip says it finds moments using visual, audio and sentiment cues, and recommends it for videos with little or no talking, like sports, gaming or vlogs. For interviews and podcasts, the talking is what matters.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Pick a genre and set the options","text":"Selecting your video genre is optional. Set the clip length here too: by default it is Auto, which means clips of up to 3 minutes. Prompts cannot change clip length, so set it in this box.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Type a prompt (optional)","text":"Write what you want in plain English. A good prompt names the subject, the action and the feeling or sound you are looking for. The examples below come from OpusClip's own prompt manual.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: The safe default","text":"Find the moments most likely to go viral on social media","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: For podcasts and interviews","text":"Show me moments with strong opinions or words","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: For product videos","text":"Show me the host unboxing a new tech gadget and explaining its features","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: For a compilation","text":"Find all the scenes with laughter","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Pick a caption style","text":"Choose a style from Quick Presets, or select No Caption if your video already has subtitles or you want a clean look. Save your favorite model, genre and preset as defaults so you do not set them every time.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Review, rate and edit","text":"Each clip gets a virality score, the tool's guess of how likely it is to do well. You can sort clips by score or by the order they appear in the video. Download or schedule","text":"Download the clip, or connect your social accounts and schedule it. Pro users can also export XML files to keep editing in Adobe Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What prompts cannot do","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpusClip's manual is clear about the limits. Prompts find moments, they do not edit them. A prompt cannot clean up audio, change the aspect ratio, add emojis or transitions, or set clip length. Vague prompts like \"Create videos\" or \"Do it\" do not work, and prompts should be written in English. The manual also says it works better to describe what you want than what you do not want.","sources":[{"name":"OpusClip Help Center: ClipAnything prompt manual","url":"https://help.opus.pro/docs/article/clip-anything-prompt-manual.md"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Be specific about what is on screen. \"The woman in the yellow dress\" or \"audience cheering\" gives the model something it can actually look and listen for.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the free plan is good for","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For trying the tool out, it works. A CNET writer who tested the free plan said a video of just over two minutes took about five minutes to process, and one clip scored 85 percent for virality. The same test pointed out the downsides: free clips carry the OpusClip watermark and the credits run out quickly.","sources":[{"name":"CNET via AOL: How to use AI to edit videos into short clips","url":"https://www.aol.com/ai-edit-videos-short-clips-120011417.html"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The honest math: 60 free credits is one hour of source video a month. That is one podcast episode or a few short streams. If you post clips every day, you will hit the limit in the first week, and the watermark makes free clips look like free clips. Start with your best long video, use the timeframe slider, and only pay once you know the clips actually perform for your account.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"The virality score is a guess, not a promise. Watch every clip before you post it. A clip that starts mid sentence or cuts off the punch line will flop no matter what score it got.","sources":[]}]}

Edit the instructions","text":"Once the agent is set up, change its name, description and instructions on the Overview page. This is where you set the tone and the rules. item.title: An AI agent did a man's grocery shopping and sent him 72 eggs he never asked for
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Matt Smith wrote: "Today an LLM hallucination resulted in 72 eggs being delivered to my house. 🥚🥚🥚🥚" Matt Smith of investment firm Rebellionaire had an AI agent handle his groceries. It put 4 cartons of Vital Farms pasture-raised large eggs, 18 each, in the cart he checked out. There was no line for eggs on his list. Asked why it chose four cartons, the agent said it could not find any note explaining the choice. Then it admitted the eggs were never on the list. "Then I added them without any reason, and that's on me." Sources: Futurism, Digital Focus, Matt Smith on X.

Korean outlet Digital Focus, which also covered the incident, said the agent completed the purchase and that Smith's post was dated November 10.","sources":[{"name":"Futurism","url":"https://futurism.com/artificial-intelligence/ai-agent-cant-explain-egg-order"},{"name":"Digital Focus","url":"https://www.digitalfocus.news/news/articleView.html?idxno=25183"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The agent's explanation","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"When Smith asked why it chose four cartons, the agent replied that it did not have a good answer and could not find any note explaining the choice, Futurism reported. Smith described it as the first time he had experienced a real-world consequence of a hallucination by a large language model.","sources":[{"name":"Futurism","url":"https://futurism.com/artificial-intelligence/ai-agent-cant-explain-egg-order"},{"name":"Digital Focus","url":"https://www.digitalfocus.news/news/articleView.html?idxno=25183"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Neither report named the AI model or agent platform involved, the grocery store that filled the order, or the total cost of the eggs.","sources":[{"name":"Futurism","url":"https://futurism.com/artificial-intelligence/ai-agent-cant-explain-egg-order"},{"name":"Digital Focus","url":"https://www.digitalfocus.news/news/articleView.html?idxno=25183"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Why a small error matters","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Digital Focus noted that once AI agents hold payment authority, errors of this kind can quickly turn into financial losses. item.title: Eric Trump-backed war robot startup missed payroll. Its CEO had borrowed $4.6 million from the company
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Foundation Future Industries builds Phantom humanoid robots for defense. It missed its October 30 payroll, and staff had still not been paid, CNBC reported. CEO Sankaet Pathak told employees he was working to find the money. Pathak borrowed $4.6 million from the company. An LLC with him as sole principal bought a $4.6 million home in Sausalito, California, in October 2025. He is also the company's only board member. item.title: How to make AI videos in Gemini, step by step
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On gemini.google.com, open the sidebar and pick Create video. Type a prompt, add up to five images or one video, then Submit. It takes a few minutes. You need a Google AI plan and must be 18 or older. Clips run 3 to 10 seconds, or up to 15 with AI Ultra. Video uses more of your limit than anything else. Sources: Gemini Apps Help: Generate videos with Gemini Apps, Gemini Apps Help: Gemini Apps limits and upgrades for Google AI subscribers, Google: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, The Next Web, Android Central.

Google may refuse to make a video, or remove it, if it detects a possible violation.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Generate videos with Gemini Apps","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16126339"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The short version: if you already pay for a Google AI plan, Create video in Gemini is the easiest way to try Omni, and the edit-by-chat loop is where it earns its keep. item.title: How to use Hugging Face to find and try AI models
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Spaces are AI demo apps that run in your browser. The Hub hosts over 2 million of them. No code and no install: open one and try it. Sources: Hugging Face Hub documentation, Hugging Face docs: Inference Providers on the Hub, Hugging Face docs: Inference Providers pricing, Hugging Face docs: Gated models, Techopedia: What is Hugging Face.

Models are the AI models themselves, for text, images, audio and more. Datasets are collections of data for training and testing, with over 1 million public ones in more than 8,000 languages. Spaces are interactive apps that show a model working directly in your browser.","sources":[{"name":"Hugging Face Hub documentation","url":"https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/index.md"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Every model page has a model card, which describes what the model does and its known limitations and biases. Some model pages also have an inference widget, a small box where you can type an input and see the result without leaving the page.","sources":[{"name":"Hugging Face Hub documentation","url":"https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/index.md"},{"name":"Hugging Face docs: Inference Providers on the Hub","url":"https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/models-inference.md"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to try models on Hugging Face without writing code","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Compare chat models in the Inference Playground","text":"The Inference Playground at huggingface.co/playground lets you test chat models with your own prompts and compare them. It is the quickest way to see how an open model handles the kind of question you actually ask.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Widgets and the Playground both run on Inference Providers, a pay as you go service.  model="[model id, for example deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324]",
 messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "[your prompt]"}]
)
print(completion.choices[0].message.content)","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The provider setting auto picks a provider for you. Most strong prompts include most of these.","sources":[{"name":"Leonardo.Ai Help: How to write great text-to-image prompts","url":"https://intercom.help/leonardo-ai/en/articles/8942657-how-to-write-great-text-to-image-prompts"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Leonardo's own five-part example","text":"Realistic oil painting of a grumpy man in a seated pose, slightly off-center, focusing on facial expressions, with natural, muted colors and soft ambient lighting","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: The same pattern for a product photo","text":"Photograph of [your product] on a [surface], centered, shot from slightly above, clean minimal style, with soft daylight from the left and a pale [color] background","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: The same pattern for a social post","text":"Flat digital illustration of [subject] doing [action], bold graphic style, subject on the left third with empty space on the right for text, bright [color] and [color] palette with even lighting","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"For ideas, leave the prompt bar empty, click the dice icon and choose New Random Prompt. Or type a short idea like an orange cat and use Improve Prompt, then look at which details it added. Both are free ways to learn what the models respond to.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Open images in the Community Feed and click them to see the prompts behind them. It is the fastest way to find a style you like and copy its structure, not its exact words.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Leonardo also says that even a strong prompt often gets an image about 95% right. Fix the rest with the Canvas editor instead of spending more tokens on new attempts. Canvas supports inpainting, which regenerates only a selected area, and outpainting, which extends the borders.","sources":[{"name":"Leonardo.Ai Help: How to write great text-to-image prompts","url":"https://intercom.help/leonardo-ai/en/articles/8942657-how-to-write-great-text-to-image-prompts"},{"name":"Dupple: How to use Leonardo AI","url":"https://dupple.com/learn/how-to-use-leonardo-ai"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the free plan gets you, and what it does not","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The free plan gives 150 tokens a day. They reset every 24 hours and, according to Krea's review, do not roll over, so unused tokens are lost at the reset. Paid plans get a monthly allowance instead, and paid users can buy top-up packs that never expire while the subscription is active.","sources":[{"name":"Leonardo.Ai Help: Token usage","url":"https://intercom.help/leonardo-ai/en/articles/8044033-token-usage"},{"name":"Krea: Leonardo AI review","url":"https://www.krea.ai/blog/leonardo-ai-review-is-it-free-any-good-and-how-it-compares-in-2026"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Free images are public. Private mode, which hides your generations from the public feed, is listed in the help center as a paid feature. Ownership also depends on the plan: Krea's review of the terms says paid users own their outputs, while on the free plan ownership stays with Leonardo and free users get a commercial license to their images. Read the current terms before you use a free image for a client.","sources":[{"name":"Leonardo.Ai Help: How to generate images","url":"https://intercom.help/leonardo-ai/en/articles/8942360-how-to-generate-images-with-leonardo-ai"},{"name":"Krea: Leonardo AI review","url":"https://www.krea.ai/blog/leonardo-ai-review-is-it-free-any-good-and-how-it-compares-in-2026"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Where Leonardo falls short: video and third party models eat tokens fast, so 150 a day does not go far there. Reviewers also find that Midjourney gets a strong look with less effort, while Leonardo rewards people who are willing to tweak settings and prompts. If you want quick, pretty images and do not care about privacy, the free plan is fine. If your images are for work, the public feed alone is a reason to pay or pick another tool.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"A simple daily routine for the free plan: try four or five ideas in Fast mode, pick one, fix small problems in Canvas, and only then upscale it. That keeps most of your tokens for the image you actually use.","sources":[]}]}

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Claude Design: make designs, prototypes and slides by chatting with Claude","dek":"Claude Design builds mockups, clickable prototypes and decks on a canvas next to the chat. Add your design system and some context, describe the goal and audience, then refine the canvas with chat, comments or direct edits and export it.","tags":["Claude Design","Claude","Anthropic","Guides","AI design tools"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Claude Design, in short: ask Claude for a design, give it your brand and some context, then fix the result on the canvas and export it. Claude Design is a tool from Anthropic Labs that turns a conversation into visual work: app and website mockups, interactive prototypes, slide decks and one-pagers. The work appears on a canvas beside the chat, where you keep editing it.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Get started with Claude Design","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design"},{"name":"Anthropic: Introducing Claude Design by Anthropic Labs","url":"https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-design-anthropic-labs"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic launched Claude Design on April 17, 2026 as a research preview for Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise subscribers. According to the Claude Help Center, it is now available on Free, Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise plans and is turned on by default.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Get started with Claude Design","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design"},{"name":"Anthropic: Introducing Claude Design by Anthropic Labs","url":"https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-design-anthropic-labs"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The point is speed to a first draft. If you are a founder, a product manager or anyone who has to show an idea before a designer has time for it, Claude Design gets you something clickable in minutes. It does not replace a good designer for polished, final work.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where to open Claude Design","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"There are four ways in, per the Help Center. In a normal conversation, ask for a design or choose Output, then Design. In the Artifacts tab, pick a Design template. In Claude Code, ask Claude or type /design. On the iOS and Android apps you can create, view and edit designs, but sharing settings have to be changed on the web or the desktop app.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Get started with Claude Design","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The older standalone version at claude.ai/design closes on December 14, 2026. The Help Center tells users to move their projects and design systems before then.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Get started with Claude Design","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you used Claude Design at claude.ai/design earlier this year, move your projects now instead of in December, so you have time to check nothing went missing.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Claude Design, step by step","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Start a design","text":"Open a chat and ask for a design, or go to the Artifacts tab and choose a Design template. Say what you want to make: a landing page, an app screen, a pitch deck, a one-pager.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Add a design system","text":"A design system holds your colors, typography and components, so every project looks like your brand. You can import one from a GitHub repository, design files, uploads or a local codebase with /design-sync. Projects pick up your organization's design system automatically.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Give it context","text":"Attach screenshots and other assets, or link a codebase. The more Claude can see of what already exists, the less it guesses.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Describe the goal","text":"Say what the design is for, the layout you have in mind, the content it must show and who will use it. Mention the target device (phone, laptop, projector) at the start.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Review and refine","text":"Look at the canvas, then pick the right tool for the change. Use chat for big structural changes or to ask why something was done. Use inline comments for one component. Edit the canvas directly to drag, resize or align things.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Export or share","text":"Export as a .zip, a PDF, a PowerPoint file, Google Slides or standalone HTML, send it to other tools, or hand it off to Claude Code. Designs are private by default; you can share them with view, comment or edit access.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic says the handoff to Claude Code packages the finished design into a bundle that Claude Code can build from with a single instruction. Designs can also be exported to Canva.","sources":[{"name":"Anthropic: Introducing Claude Design by Anthropic Labs","url":"https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-design-anthropic-labs"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts that get better designs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic's own tips are short: import a complete design system, start simple and add detail later, give specific feedback that names the component, mention the target device early, ask for two or three variations, and ask Claude to review accessibility and visual hierarchy.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Get started with Claude Design","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A first draft with options","text":"Design a landing page for [product] aimed at [audience]. Mobile first. Use my design system. Sections: hero with one clear headline, three benefits, pricing, a short FAQ. Give me 3 variations with different layouts.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Feedback that names the part","text":"In variation 2, make the pricing cards stack vertically on mobile, move the FAQ above the footer and make the main button in the hero larger. Keep everything else the same.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: A slide deck from your numbers","text":"Make an 8 slide deck for [meeting] from the attached file. One idea per slide, a chart where the numbers matter, presenter notes on every slide. Use my design system.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: A check before you share","text":"Review this design for accessibility and visual hierarchy. List every problem you find, from most to least important, then fix the top three.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Check every number Claude puts on a slide against your source. In a hands-on test, TechFinitive found wrong figures and a cropped screenshot in a deck Claude Design made, plus typography problems after export to PowerPoint.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Usage limits and what it is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Claude Design draws on the same usage limits as the rest of Claude, including Claude Code, according to the Help Center. Large codebases and many rounds of changes use more. When you hit the limit, Claude Design stops until the limit resets, unless usage credits are turned on.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Get started with Claude Design","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Reviewers found the limits to be the main constraint. Writing for Zapier in May 2026, Miguel Rebelo said a Pro plan's weekly allowance could run out in under an hour of work, and that without a custom design system the output tends toward a recognizable look with heavy serif fonts, cards and accent bars.","sources":[{"name":"Zapier: What is Claude Design?","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/claude-design/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic lists its own known limitations: inline comments can sometimes disappear (pasting the feedback into chat works around it), very large repositories can cause lag, editing by several people at once is basic, the quality of an imported design system depends on the source files, and there is no version history yet.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Get started with Claude Design","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Because there is no version history, export a PDF or HTML copy of any version you like before asking for big changes.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Claude Design is best treated as a fast sketching partner. Use it for a first draft, a pitch deck you need by tomorrow or a clickable prototype to test an idea. For production code, hand the design to Claude Code or a developer, and for a brand that has to look exactly right, keep a designer in the loop.","sources":[]}]}

It cannot be removed, but you can delete or reset its chats and keep it out of sensitive conversations.","seo_title":"How to use Meta AI in WhatsApp and limit what it keeps","seo_description":"How to use Meta AI in WhatsApp: chat, search bar, @Meta AI in groups, imagine prompts, Incognito Chat, and how to reset or limit it.","answer_summary":"Open the Meta AI chat or type in the WhatsApp search bar, use @Meta AI in groups and type imagine to create images. WhatsApp says these chats are processed in a secure environment Meta cannot access, are not saved and disappear by default. Meta said it would roll out over the following months, so it may not be on your phone yet.","sources":[{"name":"WhatsApp Blog: Introducing Incognito Chat with Meta AI","url":"https://blog.whatsapp.com/introducing-incognito-chat-with-meta-ai-a-completely-private-way-to-chat-with-ai"},{"name":"Meta Newsroom: Introducing a completely private way to chat with AI","url":"https://about.fb.com/news/2026/05/incognito-chat-whatsapp-meta-ai/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Message summaries, where Meta AI sums up unread messages in a chat, also run on Private Processing. WhatsApp says this feature is off by default, and you choose whether to use it.","sources":[{"name":"WhatsApp Blog: Private Message Summaries","url":"https://blog.whatsapp.com/catch-up-on-conversations-with-private-message-summaries"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Turning off Meta AI in WhatsApp: what is possible","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"No. WhatsApp calls Meta AI optional, but its help center describes no setting that turns it off or removes it from the app, and guides from Android Authority, MSPowerUser and Kanal reach the same conclusion. If you never open the Meta AI chat or mention it, it does nothing.","sources":[{"name":"WhatsApp Help Center: About Meta AI","url":"https://faq.whatsapp.com/2257017191175152"},{"name":"Kanal: Meta AI on WhatsApp, can you turn it off or remove it?","url":"https://getkanal.com/blog/meta-ai-whatsapp"},{"name":"MSPowerUser: Can you remove Meta AI from WhatsApp?","url":"https://mspoweruser.com/remove-meta-ai-whatsapp"},{"name":"Android Authority: How to turn off Meta AI","url":"https://www.androidauthority.com/turn-off-meta-ai-3437314/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"What you can do: delete individual AI chats, and ask Meta to delete information you shared with Meta AI, as WhatsApp's help center describes. Deleting a chat removes it from your device, but Kanal notes it does not erase Meta AI's copy.","sources":[{"name":"WhatsApp Help Center: About Meta AI","url":"https://faq.whatsapp.com/2257017191175152"},{"name":"WhatsApp Help Center: How to chat with Meta AI","url":"https://faq.whatsapp.com/666767195111959/?cms_platform=web"},{"name":"Kanal: Meta AI on WhatsApp, can you turn it off or remove it?","url":"https://getkanal.com/blog/meta-ai-whatsapp"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to Kanal and MSPowerUser, sending /reset-ai in a Meta AI chat deletes Meta AI's copy of that conversation, and /reset-all-ais does it for every AI chat. Kanal says these commands do not work in Incognito chats.","sources":[{"name":"Kanal: Meta AI on WhatsApp, can you turn it off or remove it?","url":"https://getkanal.com/blog/meta-ai-whatsapp"},{"name":"MSPowerUser: Can you remove Meta AI from WhatsApp?","url":"https://mspoweruser.com/remove-meta-ai-whatsapp"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For sensitive conversations, turn on Advanced Chat Privacy: tap the chat name, then Advanced Chat Privacy. WhatsApp says it stops people from exporting the chat, auto saving its media and using its messages in AI features.","sources":[{"name":"WhatsApp Blog: Introducing Advanced Chat Privacy","url":"https://blog.whatsapp.com/introducing-advanced-chat-privacy"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"For fewer pings, mute the Meta AI chat like any other chat, as Android Authority suggests. It stays in the app but stops asking for attention.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What is coming next","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In July 2026 Meta said Meta AI, powered by its Muse Spark model, can now carry out multi step tasks such as making plans, research and daily briefings. Those features started in the Meta AI app and on meta.ai, and Meta said WhatsApp would get them later.","sources":[{"name":"Meta Newsroom: Meta AI doesn't just think, it acts","url":"https://about.fb.com/news/2026/07/meta-ai-muse-spark-doesnt-just-think-it-acts/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The honest verdict: Meta AI in WhatsApp is handy for quick questions, group planning and fast images without leaving the chat. It is weaker for anything you need to be exactly right, and you cannot remove it. Use the reset commands and Advanced Chat Privacy if you care about what Meta keeps.","sources":[]}]}

LM Studio's pricing page lists a $0 Free plan for running local models on your machine, and since July 8, 2025 the company has said the app is free to use at work too, with no separate commercial license to request.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio: Pricing","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/pricing"},{"name":"LM Studio blog: LM Studio is free for use at work","url":"https://www.lmstudio.ai/blog/free-for-work"},{"name":"Simon Willison: LM Studio is free for use at work","url":"https://simonwillison.net/2025/Jul/8/lm-studio-is-free-for-use-at-work/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The reason to bother is privacy and control. Your prompts and files stay on your own hardware, and nothing stops working when your internet does. The price is speed and quality: a model that fits on a laptop is smaller than the ones behind ChatGPT or Claude, so expect simpler answers on hard tasks.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What your computer needs to run LM Studio","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Check this before you download anything. On a Mac, LM Studio needs Apple Silicon (M1 or newer) and macOS 14.0 or later; Intel Macs are not supported. The docs recommend 16 GB of RAM or more, and say 8 GB Macs can still work with smaller models and shorter context.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"On Windows, LM Studio supports x64 and ARM (Snapdragon X Elite) PCs. An x64 processor must support the AVX2 instruction set, and the docs recommend at least 16 GB of RAM and at least 4 GB of dedicated graphics memory. On Linux it ships as an AppImage for x64 and ARM64 and needs Ubuntu 20.04 or newer.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"RAM decides which models you can use. If you have 8 GB, start with the smallest models you can find and keep chats short. With 16 GB or more you have real choices.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use LM Studio: install and chat","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Download the app","text":"Go to lmstudio.ai/download and get the installer for your system. Install it like any other desktop app. The same page also offers llmster, a version with no window for servers, which most people do not need.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Find a model in Discover","text":"Open the Discover tab, or press Cmd + 2 on a Mac or Ctrl + 2 on Windows and Linux. Search by keyword, by a user/model name, or paste a full Hugging Face link. LM Studio downloads models from Hugging Face.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Pick the right size","text":"Models come in versions marked with a Q, such as Q3_K_S or Q8. The Q stands for quantization: smaller files that give up a bit of quality. The docs suggest a 4-bit option or higher if your computer can run it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Load the model and chat","text":"Open the Chat tab and use the model loader at the top (Cmd + L on a Mac, Ctrl + L on Windows and Linux). Pick the model you downloaded, wait for it to load into memory, then type your first message.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Keep your chats organized","text":"Start a new chat with the + button or Cmd + N (Ctrl + N on Windows and Linux). Group chats in folders with Cmd + Shift + N, drag them around, or duplicate one from the three-dot menu to try a different question from the same point. You can also drag two chats side by side in split view.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Your downloaded models live in the My Models tab, which is also where you change the folder LM Studio saves them to.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Models take many gigabytes. If your main drive is small, point the models folder at an external or second drive in My Models before you download several.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Chat with your own files, offline","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"You can attach .docx, .pdf and .txt files to a chat and ask questions about them. If the document fits in the model's context, LM Studio adds the whole text to the conversation. If it is too long, it switches to retrieval (RAG) and pulls in only the parts that look relevant to your question.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"},{"name":"LM Studio docs: Chat with Documents","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/docs/app/basics/rag"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to the docs, document processing happens on your computer and nothing you upload leaves the app. Context is measured in tokens, and one token is often about three quarters of a word.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"},{"name":"LM Studio docs: Chat with Documents","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/docs/app/basics/rag"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"That makes LM Studio a decent fit for private papers: a contract, medical bills, notes from work. The limit is the honest one: with long files, retrieval can miss the part you need, so ask specific questions and name the section when you can.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Save your instructions with presets","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A preset bundles a system prompt and other settings into one reusable setup. Use the presets dropdown in the sidebar and choose + New Preset. Presets can also be imported from a file or a link.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"A system prompt worth saving as a preset","text":"You are a careful assistant running on my own computer. Answer in plain English and keep it short. If you are not sure about a fact, say so instead of guessing. When I paste a document, quote the exact line your answer comes from.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Use LM Studio as a local server","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"LM Studio can serve your models on OpenAI-like endpoints, so apps and scripts that talk to the OpenAI API can talk to your local model instead. The default address is http://localhost:1234. You can start the server from the app or from a terminal.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs: Welcome","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/docs/app"},{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"The lms commands that matter","text":"lms get [model]
lms load [model]
lms ls
lms ps
lms server start --port 1234
lms chat
lms unload --all","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"In order: lms get downloads a model, lms load puts it in memory, lms ls lists models on disk, lms ps lists loaded ones, lms server start runs the server, lms chat opens a chat in the terminal and lms unload frees the memory again.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"LM Studio can also act as an MCP host since version 0.3.17, so local models can use tools from MCP servers. You add them in the Program tab of the right sidebar under Install, then Edit mcp.json. The docs warn that some MCP servers can run code, read local files and use your network, so install only ones you trust.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio docs (full text: system requirements, downloading models, chats, CLI, MCP)","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What LM Studio costs, and what Bionic is","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Local use is on the free plan. LM Studio now also offers Bionic, an agent for open models built on the LM Studio runtime that can write code, make documents and automate tasks. Its paid plans add models hosted in the US: Bionic+ costs $20 a month and Pro costs $100 a month with five times the usage limits.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio: Pricing","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/pricing"},{"name":"LM Studio: Download","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/download"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"For most people the free app is the whole point. Pay only if you want bigger open models than your computer can run, and at that point compare the price with the ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini plans you may already have.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Ollama to run AI models on your own computer
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In the Ollama app on Mac, open Apps and turn on Claude. Claude Desktop then runs the model you pick in Ollama. Turn it off to go back to your old setup. Local models need no account or API key. Ollama's cloud models have a small free monthly allowance. Pro costs $20 a month and includes $60 of usage. Sources: Ollama docs: Quickstart, Ollama docs: CLI reference, Ollama: Download, Ollama blog: Transparent pricing, Ollama blog: Claude Desktop support, LLM Hardware: Ollama cheat sheet.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Ollama to run AI models on your own computer, step by step","dek":"Ollama downloads open models and runs them locally with one command. Here is how to install it, which commands matter and how much memory you need.","summary":"Ollama is a free app for Mac, Windows and Linux that runs open AI models on your own computer and needs no account for local use. It can also plug local models into Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex, and offers paid cloud models.","seo_title":"How to use Ollama to run AI models on your own computer","seo_description":"How to use Ollama: install it, run your first model with one command, manage models, check memory needs and connect it to Claude and Codex.","answer_summary":"Install Ollama from ollama.com/download, open a terminal and type ollama run gemma4:e2b. Ollama downloads the model and starts a chat on your own computer; type /bye to leave. Local models need no account or API key.","tags":["Ollama","Local AI","Open models","Guides","Gemma"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to use Ollama, in short: download it from ollama.com/download, open a terminal and type ollama run followed by a model name. Ollama downloads the model and starts a chat that runs on your own computer. It is available for macOS, Windows and Linux, and local models need no account and no API key.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama docs: Quickstart","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/quickstart"},{"name":"Ollama: Download","url":"https://ollama.com/download"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The appeal is privacy and control. A local model runs on your own hardware, so your prompts do not have to leave it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Ollama also sells cloud models, and it can connect models to tools such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama docs: Quickstart","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/quickstart"},{"name":"Ollama blog: Transparent pricing","url":"https://ollama.com/blog/transparent-pricing"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to install Ollama","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Download it","text":"Go to ollama.com/download and pick macOS, Windows or Linux. On Linux the page gives a one-line install command that you paste into a terminal.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Linux install command","text":"curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Run the setup","text":"Open the app, or type ollama in a terminal and follow the prompts. During setup you either sign in to use cloud models or choose a local model.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"You can skip the sign-in if you only want local models. The docs say an account and API key are needed only for Ollama's cloud models.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Run your first model in Ollama","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Ollama's own quickstart uses gemma4:e2b, a small version of Gemma 4. The download is about 7.2 GB, and Ollama recommends about 8 GB of free graphics memory, or unified memory on a Mac. With less, Ollama falls back to system memory and answers get slower.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama docs: Quickstart","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/quickstart"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Command 1: Download and chat","text":"ollama run gemma4:e2b","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Chat and leave","text":"Type your question after the prompt and press Enter. Type /bye when you are done. To paste several lines as one message, start and end the block with three quote marks.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Command 2: Ask about an image","text":"ollama run gemma4 \"What's in this image? [path to your picture]\"","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Put a prompt right after the model name, as in the image example, to get a one-off answer without opening a chat.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The Ollama commands you will actually use","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Ollama's CLI reference lists a short set of commands: ollama pull downloads a model without starting it, ollama ls lists downloaded models, ollama ps shows what is running, ollama stop unloads a model and ollama rm deletes it from disk.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama docs: CLI reference","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/cli.md"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Command 3: Clean up disk space","text":"ollama ls\nollama rm [model name]","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"LLM Hardware's cheat sheet adds a useful check: ollama ps shows how much of a model sits on the graphics card. Below 100 percent means part of it spilled to the processor, and speed can drop to roughly 1 to 5 tokens per second.","sources":[{"name":"LLM Hardware: Ollama cheat sheet","url":"https://llmhardware.io/guides/ollama-cheat-sheet"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Ollama only listens on your own computer by default. Longer conversations need more on top of that.","sources":[{"name":"LLM Hardware: Ollama cheat sheet","url":"https://llmhardware.io/guides/ollama-cheat-sheet"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"For most laptops that means small models. They are fine for summaries, rewriting and simple questions, but they are not as sharp as the big cloud assistants. Start small and move up only if your machine keeps up.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Connect Ollama to Claude, Codex and other apps","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"Claude Desktop","text":"In the Ollama app on a Mac, open Apps and turn on Claude. Ollama sets up the connection, and you choose the model in Ollama. The quickstart says ollama launch also works with codex and opencode, and Ollama offers to install Claude Code or OpenCode if they are missing. Codex has to be installed first.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama docs: Quickstart","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/quickstart"},{"name":"Ollama docs: CLI reference","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/cli.md"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Ollama free plan and cloud prices","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Local use is free.
